sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record lumb1237 'Lumbee' (category Unattested; ISO 639-3 lmz retired 2020-01-23 by CR 2019-025, reason 'non-existent'; only ref: Wolfram & Dannenberg 1999, med 'a wordlist or less')
sources.note: Nothing; it is a catalog record stating the languoid is unattested and its ISO code was retired as non-existent.

sources.citation: Wikipedia articles 'Lumbee' and 'Lumbee English' (read online for orientation only)
sources.note: State that the Lumbee speak English (Lumbee English) and that no Native American language of the Lumbee is recorded; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blu, Karen I. 2004. Lumbee. In Raymond D. Fogelson (ed.), Southeast (Handbook of North American Indians 14), 278-295. Washington, D.C.: Smithsonian Institution.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Handbook chapter likely to summarize what is known of the Lumbee's linguistic history (i.e. that no ancestral language is attested); ethnographic, no phonology.

sources.citation: Wolfram, Walt & Clare Dannenberg. 1999. Dialect identity in a tri-ethnic context: the case of Lumbee American Indian English. English World-Wide 20(2): 179-216.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only linguistic source Glottolog lists for the languoid; describes Lumbee English (a dialect of English), not an indigenous language. Full text would confirm whether it discusses the lost ancestral language at all; no word-stress rule for a non-English language is expected.

sources.citation: Lowery, Malinda Maynor. 2010. Lumbee Indians in the Jim Crow South: race, identity, and the making of a nation. Chapel Hill: UNC Press. (hh.bib e:Lowery:Lumbee, listed by Glottolog as an ethnographic work)
